picks.rationale: Caine Prize closes its AI-authorship review: no evidence the winning story was AI-generated, winner confirmed. This is the official outcome of the 10-13 accusation story.
picks.excerpt: The Caine Prize's review found no evidence that Simbarashe Kundizeza's winning story 'The Blue Fighter' was AI-generated and confirmed him as 2026 winner; he had denied the allegation made in a US magazine.

picks.rationale: New court filing: SAG-AFTRA, AFM and WGA seek to file a brief in the OpenAI copyright case, putting audiobook narrators' lost work (NAVA survey) on the record.
picks.excerpt: SAG-AFTRA, AFM and the WGA asked to file a brief in the OpenAI copyright case, citing a NAVA survey of voice actors (including audiobook narrators) losing work to synthetic voices.

picks.rationale: Hands-on: a reader used Claude to build custom apps for a jailbroken 7th-gen Kindle. This is a different project from the 11-08 offline-LLM Kindle hack.
picks.excerpt: A hobbyist used Anthropic's Claude to build custom apps for a jailbroken 7th-gen Kindle, turning the e-reader into a device that does far more than display books.

picks.rationale: A concrete new deal: five K-webtoon IPs licensed for Chinese AI short-drama production, with release set for November. It shows a new AI adaptation route for comics IP.
picks.excerpt: 자주스토리가 한국 웹툰 원작 IP 5종을 활용한 중국 AI 숏드라마 제작 계약을 완료하고 11월 공개를 준비한다.

picks.rationale: How Korean audiobook producers actually split the work: AI narration fills the commercially unviable backlist, while flagship titles still go to human actors.
picks.excerpt: Korean audiobook producers mainly use AI narration to fill gaps — audio versions of books otherwise commercially unviable — while flagship titles still go to human voice actors.
